title: Total evapotranspiration and fractionating isotopes leave storage scale unresolved when plant uptake can shift between stores
abstract: We test whether total evapotranspiration and two water isotopes can separate recharge from store loss. For a mixed store with a fixed linear stream relation of unknown scale, flexible non-negative plant uptake and liquid leakage leave an exact interval of storage scales. This holds even when fractionating evaporation and isotope input concentrations are known. We derive sharp bounds from water balance and non-negative fluxes. A synthetic experiment checks the family with independent water and tracer mass integrations. A known store evaporation flux or a suitable total vapor isotope measurement removes the ambiguity. Constant export coefficients can also remove it under variable forcing. This is a model and measurement-design result. It does not locate the missing water in south-east Australia. It assumes complete mixing, no upstream storage change, exact observations and flexible loss laws. Proof, code, synthetic inputs, bounds tool, controls and audits are included.

display.caption: Synthetic stores and plant uptake differ while flow, both stream isotope records and total evapotranspiration stay fixed. The interval follows from non-negative fluxes. The black line shows the scale fixed by a known store flux.
